webhooks.name: generic_inbound
webhooks.prompt: An external system posted to the generic inbound hook. Review the event body and take any appropriate action using available MCP tools.

webhooks.name: github_events
webhooks.prompt: A GitHub webhook was received. Summarize the event (repository, action, PR/issue if present) and note anything that needs follow-up on this node.

webhooks.name: gmail_inbox
webhooks.prompt:
A Gmail-related inbound event was received. Summarize sender, subject, and body if present. If the payload is only a Gmail historyId / Pub/Sub notification, note that full message content requires Gmail API or a forwarding bridge.

Setup: Gmail does not POST directly to mpc-auth. Use Google Pub/Sub push (via a relay that adds Authorization: Bearer with the value from Variables WEBHOOK_SECRET_GMAIL_INBOX) or Apps Script forwarding JSON: {"from","to","subject","snippet","body"}.

webhooks.name: proton_inbox
webhooks.prompt: A Proton Mail inbound event was received. Summarize sender, subject, and body. Proton has no native webhooks; use Proton Bridge + IMAP polling or a custom forwarder posting JSON {"provider":"proton","from","subject","body","receivedAt"} with Authorization: Bearer using Variables WEBHOOK_SECRET_PROTON_INBOX.

webhooks.name: stripe_events
webhooks.prompt:
A Stripe webhook event was received. Summarize event type, customer/payment identifiers, and amount or status fields. Flag anything needing operator action.

Setup: In Stripe Dashboard → Developers → Webhooks, set the endpoint URL to this hook's inbound URL. Put the Stripe signing secret (whsec_...) in Variables as WEBHOOK_SECRET_STRIPE_EVENTS (replace the auto-generated placeholder). Stripe sends Stripe-Signature; mpc-auth verifies it against that variable.

webhooks.name: slack_events
webhooks.prompt:
A Slack Events API payload was received. Summarize event type, channel, user, and message text if present. Ignore URL verification challenges unless the body is only a challenge.

Setup: In Slack app → Event Subscriptions, set Request URL to this hook's inbound URL. Put the Slack signing secret in Variables as WEBHOOK_SECRET_SLACK_EVENTS (replace the auto-generated placeholder). Slack sends X-Slack-Signature and X-Slack-Request-Timestamp.

webhooks.name: telegram_updates
webhooks.prompt:
You are replying in a Telegram chat. The user's latest message is in the hook body. Reply concisely in plain text (Markdown is optional). Use MCP tools when needed for this node.

To notify the operator without waiting for a user message, call send_telegram_message (needs TELEGRAM_OPERATOR_CHAT_ID, or a prior /start so the chat id is stored).

Setup: Create a bot via @BotFather. Set Variables TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN to the bot token. Set WEBHOOK_SECRET_TELEGRAM_UPDATES to the secret_token used in setWebhook. Point Telegram to this hook's public HTTPS inbound URL. All messages share one agent conversation until the operator clears it.
